conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, Mr. Thompson. I’m Dr. Lee, one of the vascular surgery team. You’ve been admitted today because we found a narrowing in the artery that supplies blood to your transplanted kidney. We’re planning to do a procedure to open it up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, doctor. I’ve had this before, right? Last year they put in a stent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, exactly. The stent is still there, but it’s developed a narrowing inside — what we call in-stent restenosis. That’s why your blood pressure has been going up lately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Ah, that makes sense. My nurse at home said my pressures were high. So what are we going to do now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll do a balloon angioplasty. We go through a small puncture in your groin, thread a catheter up to the kidney artery, and use a balloon to reopen the narrowed area.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I be asleep? I remember last time I was groggy afterward.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll be under light sedation — not fully asleep, but relaxed and comfortable. The procedure is minimally invasive and usually goes very smoothly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And is it safe with my transplant and diabetes?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ve taken all that into account. You’ve been pre-hydrated to protect your kidney, and we’ve coordinated with transplant nephrology. Your labs look good, and your blood sugar is stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve been checking it like they told me. What about the medications I’m on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll continue all your usual meds — especially your immunosuppressants like tacrolimus and mycophenolate. We’ll also keep your insulin and blood pressure pills.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And after the procedure? Will I feel better right away?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Many patients notice their blood pressure improves quickly. But the main goal is to protect your kidney function over time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. How long will I be here?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Most people stay one to two days. We’ll watch you closely after the procedure, and if all goes well, you could go home tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright, that sounds manageable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Mr. Thompson, we’re about to head down to the endovascular suite. Any last questions before we start?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, doctor. I trust you. Just let me know when it’s done.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Will do. You’ll wake up in the recovery area, and I’ll come talk to you afterward.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi again. You’re in the recovery unit. The procedure went perfectly. We opened up the narrowed part of the artery with the balloon. No complications.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great to hear. Is the stent still okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The stent is intact. The narrowing was inside it, so we dilated it with the balloon. We didn’t need to place a new stent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my kidney? Is it getting good blood flow now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the angiogram showed much better flow after the angioplasty. That should help your kidney function and keep your blood pressure more stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. My brother had a heart stent — he’s on two blood thinners. Will I need that too?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, actually. You’ll be on aspirin and Plavix — that’s clopidogrel — for at least a few months to prevent clots from forming in the stent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I can do that. Any side effects I should watch for?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Mainly bleeding — like if you notice bruising, nosebleeds, or blood in your stool. But it’s uncommon. We’ll keep the dose low to minimize risk.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. What about the groin spot where they went in?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It should heal quickly. Keep it clean and dry. You can shower tomorrow. Avoid heavy lifting for about a week to let it seal properly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No lifting — like how much?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nothing over five pounds — so no grocery bags, tools, or grandkids for a week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Ha, I’ll tell my wife. What about driving?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hold off until you’re off pain meds. Probably a few days. Just to be safe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’re doing well. Vital signs are stable, and your labs show your kidney function is unchanged — which is good news.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I can go home today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, if you’re feeling up to it. We’ll get your discharge papers ready. You’ll need to follow up with vascular surgery in two weeks for an ultrasound.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my transplant doctor too?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, definitely. Keep all your regular appointments. They’ll monitor your kidney and adjust meds as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright, doctor. Thank you — I feel much better knowing we caught this early.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re very welcome. You did great. Just take it easy for a few days, watch the incision, and call us if anything seems off — like swelling, fever, or bleeding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care, Mr. Thompson. Get some rest at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I plan to — maybe even put my feet up like you said.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. That’s exactly what I like to hear.
